title: Where accountability starts
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When did you first learn to be accountable for a habit?
I asked when accountability for our habits starts. A student answered: from six months old, depending on what the baby sees.
I said it starts in childhood: parents from an early age structure the concept of accountability, and the momentum carries into adulthood. I said I was not criticizing parents in general.
A student said: the awareness of my bad habits is driven by guilt. I asked: who installed that guilt?
Another said: there was repetitive shame, not told once but drilled into me every day. I might have made a decision once, but I would be hearing about it for four years.
I said: the parents are taking responsibility from you. They are not giving you choices, which makes you less responsible and, later, less confident to decide on your own.
I described two kinds of parents: one says do this, the other says you have a choice, you can be organized or disorganized. The second shifts the responsibility and decision to the child.

I asked what a parent is doing when they ask: why are you thinking about going out without a coat? A student said: giving the chance to think and make a decision. Another said: questioning the thought process to make it seem reasonable.
A student said: if children are told I told you so afterwards, they will double down and stay cold, because it is less painful than going back in and being ridiculed.
Education, not advice. If this is heavy for you, a trained person can help.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a habit that came from how you were raised.
Write who first held you accountable and how.
Write a choice you were given as a child, or not.
Write how you give others choices now.
Write what you will say instead of I told you so.

check.q: What did I say starts in childhood?
choices: The concept of accountability for habits

check.q: What did I say taking away choices does?
What did a student say happens after I told you so?

recap: Accountability starts early. Give choices. Do not shame.
